notice: Handwritten demonstration content for the built-in synthetic dataset. It is not model output, not ResultsCX material, and not an organization's policy.
summary: This demonstration analysis covers four QA requirements with failed items in the invented dataset. Two are coaching candidates with medium confidence (identity verification and case-note documentation), one looks like a tool problem rather than a training need (recording disclosure), and one is a low-confidence coaching candidate (confirming next steps). It was written by hand to show the workflow; no model produced it.
open_questions: Are the current verification steps clear in the call-handling tool?
Is the recording-disclosure prompt missing for other employees as well?
Do handle-time targets affect how calls are closed?

cases.behavior: Confirm identity before discussing account details

finding.title: Account details discussed before identity verification was complete
finding.observed: On three evaluations the evaluator recorded that verification was skipped or left unfinished before the account was discussed. One employee missed the step on two separate evaluations.
finding.root_cause: In two of the three comments the caller opened with a specific request and the employee began answering it before verifying. That suggests the step is known but is dropped when a call starts with a question. This reading rests on three comments and has not been confirmed with the employees.
finding.pattern: Two of four employees, one of them twice.
finding.curriculum_note: Week 1 / Day 2 'Identity verification' covers the required identifiers. Nothing in the outline practises holding verification when the caller opens with a request.
finding.confidence_note: Three failed items from two employees. The comments do not say which verification step was missed, and the cause could differ between the two employees.
corrective_actions: Practise completing verification before acknowledging any account detail, using a caller who opens with a specific request.
Coach the employee who missed the step twice individually before the group practice.
Ask the compliance owner to confirm the current verification steps so the practice matches them.

module.module_title: Verify first: holding identity verification when the caller opens with a request
module.learning_objective: By the end of this session the employee completes every identity-verification step before acknowledging or sharing any account, plan, claim, or benefit detail, including when the caller opens with a specific question.
module.why_this_fixes_the_gap: The failed evaluations describe account details being discussed before verification was finished. The practice repeats that exact moment until verifying first is the default response.
instruction: State the rule in one sentence: no account detail is acknowledged or shared until verification is complete.
Acknowledge the caller's request without confirming anything about the account, then move straight to verification.
Ask the verification questions in the organization's approved order and wait for each answer.
If the caller cannot answer, follow the approved alternative path or stop. Do not fill in or hint at the answer.
If the caller pushes back, explain that verification protects their information and continue.
Only after verification, restate the request and begin helping.
existing_material_to_reuse: Week 1 / Day 2 / Identity verification: Confirm required identifiers before discussing account details.

knowledge_check.question: A caller says, "I'm calling about the update to my plan. Did it go through?" before you have verified their identity. What do you do first?
options: A) Tell them the update went through, then verify their identity
B) Acknowledge the request and complete identity verification before confirming anything about the account
C) Ask what the update was so you can look it up while you verify
D) Verify only if the caller sounds unsure
knowledge_check.feedback: Confirming that an update exists is already an account detail, so verification comes before any confirmation. Option C is tempting, but it starts the account discussion before the caller is verified.

additional_knowledge_checks.question: During identity verification the caller cannot answer one of the required questions and asks you for a hint. What is the right response?
options: A) Use the approved alternative verification step, or explain that you cannot continue without verification
B) Give the first part of the answer so they can complete it
C) Skip that question because the other answers were correct
additional_knowledge_checks.feedback: A hint or a skipped question means verification was not completed. The approved alternative path exists for this situation.

additional_knowledge_checks.question: A caller says they are the member's spouse and asks about a recent claim before any identity verification. Which response meets the requirement?
options: A) Share the claim status because a spouse is family
B) Share the claim status once the caller gives the member's date of birth
C) Explain that you must confirm the caller is verified and permitted to receive the information before discussing the claim
additional_knowledge_checks.feedback: Being related to the member does not establish who the caller is or whether they may receive account information. Your organization's approved procedure decides that, not the call.

hands_on_exercise.title: Three openings, verify first each time
hands_on_exercise.trainee_instructions: Take three practice calls in a row. Each caller opens with a different request: a plan update, a claim question, and an address change. Respond to each opening and complete verification before anything else.
hands_on_exercise.facilitator_instructions: Play the caller. On the second call, push back once ("I'm in a hurry, can you just tell me?"). Rate each success criterion after every call and give feedback before the next one.
success_criteria: Acknowledges the request without confirming any account detail
Completes every verification step before discussing the account
Does not hint at or fill in a verification answer
Stays courteous when the caller pushes back

policy_refresher.summary: The QA requirement is scored Yes only when every verification step is complete before any account, plan, claim, or benefit detail is acknowledged or shared.
key_points: Acknowledging that something exists on the account counts as sharing an account detail.
Every step is required. A skipped or hinted answer means verification was not completed.
When the caller cannot verify, use the approved alternative path or do not proceed.

The rule for callers who say they are acting for the member.

coaching_notes.opening: Start from the call, not the score: "I'd like to walk through the start of this call with you and hear how it felt from your side."

At what point did you start verification?

The employee stays courteous when the caller pushes back.

Raise any call where verification could not be completed.

cases.behavior: Document the resolution and next steps accurately

finding.title: Case notes missing the next action, owner, or promised date
finding.observed: On four evaluations the evaluator recorded case notes that left out the next action, the follow-up owner, or a date promised to the member. Three of four employees were affected, one of them twice.
finding.root_cause: Each comment names a different missing element, which suggests employees are not working from a shared definition of a complete note rather than forgetting one specific step. This is an inference from four comments.
finding.pattern: Three of four employees, one of them twice.
finding.curriculum_note: Week 2 / Day 3 'Documentation' lists what to record, but the outline shows no worked example of a complete note.
finding.confidence_note: Four failed items across three employees give a consistent picture, but the comments do not show the notes themselves.
corrective_actions: Agree a four-part checklist for a complete note: resolution, next action, owner, date.
Review one real note per employee against the checklist in the coaching conversation.
Ask operations whether the notes template can prompt for the owner and the date.

module.module_title: A complete case note: resolution, next action, owner, date
module.learning_objective: By the end of this session the employee writes a case note that states what was resolved, the next action, who owns it, and any date promised to the member, before closing the interaction.
module.why_this_fixes_the_gap: Each failed evaluation is a note with one of those four elements missing. Practising against a fixed four-part checklist gives every employee the same definition of complete.
instruction: Introduce the four parts of a complete note: resolution, next action, owner, date.
Show one incomplete note and have the employee name what is missing.
Write the note before ending the interaction, while the details are fresh.
Record a promised date exactly as it was given to the member.
Name the team or person who owns the next action, not just 'follow-up needed'.
Read the note back against the four parts before closing.
existing_material_to_reuse: Week 2 / Day 3 / Documentation: Record the resolution, next step, and follow-up owner.

knowledge_check.question: Which case note documents the resolution and next steps accurately?
options: A) Member called about a billing question. Discussed and resolved.
B) Explained the billing adjustment. Next: billing team to confirm the corrected amount. Promised the member a call back by the 14th.
C) Member was satisfied at the end of the call. No further notes needed.
D) Billing issue. Follow-up needed.
knowledge_check.feedback: Only B states the resolution, the next action, who owns it, and the date promised. D is the tempting one: it mentions a follow-up but not what, who, or when.

additional_knowledge_checks.question: You told the member that the claims team will call them back by Friday. Which detail must appear in the case note?
options: A) That the member was polite
B) How long the call lasted
C) The Friday call-back date and that the claims team owns it
additional_knowledge_checks.feedback: A date promised to the member and the owner of the next action are both part of a complete note. Without them the next person cannot keep the promise.

additional_knowledge_checks.question: A call ends with the issue resolved and nothing left to do. What should the note say about next steps?
options: A) State the resolution and that no further action is required
B) Nothing, because there are none
C) 'Follow-up needed' in case something comes up
additional_knowledge_checks.feedback: Saying that no action is required is itself the next-step information. A blank looks unfinished, and a vague 'follow-up needed' creates work that does not exist.

hands_on_exercise.title: Complete the note
hands_on_exercise.trainee_instructions: Read three short fictional interaction summaries. For each one, write the case note using the four parts: resolution, next action, owner, date.
hands_on_exercise.facilitator_instructions: Check each note against the four parts. Where a part is missing, ask the employee what the next person reading the note would need to know.
success_criteria: States the next action, or that none is required
Names who owns the next action
Records any date promised to the member

cases.behavior: Read the required call recording disclosure

finding.title: Recording disclosure not read: prompt reported missing from the call tool
finding.observed: One evaluation was scored No because the recording disclosure was not read. The evaluator noted the employee's report that the disclosure prompt did not appear in the call-handling tool. On a later evaluation the same employee read the disclosure from memory and noted the prompt was still missing.
finding.root_cause: Both comments point to the tool not showing the prompt rather than the employee not knowing the requirement: the employee read the disclosure unprompted on the later call. If the prompt is missing for other employees, more misses are likely. Nobody has checked the tool itself.
finding.curriculum_note: Week 1 / Day 1 'Call opening' covers the recording disclosure.
finding.confidence_note: One failed item. The explanation depends on the employee's report, which has not been verified against the tool.
corrective_actions: Ask operations to check whether the disclosure prompt is displaying for all employees.
Until it is fixed, remind the team to read the disclosure from the quick-reference card.
Re-evaluate once the prompt is confirmed working.

cases.not_a_training_problem: Recording disclosure (F3): the evidence points to a prompt missing from the call-handling tool. Training would not fix a tool that does not display the prompt.

module.module_title: Read the recording disclosure on every call, with or without the prompt
module.learning_objective: By the end of this session the employee reads the call recording disclosure at the start of every call, including when the tool does not display the prompt.
module.why_this_fixes_the_gap: The failed evaluation happened when the prompt was missing. Until the tool is fixed, the disclosure has to be read without relying on it.
instruction: Read the disclosure at the start of the call, before the reason for the call is discussed.
Keep the approved disclosure wording on a quick-reference card.
If the prompt does not appear, read from the card and report the missing prompt after the call.
Do not paraphrase the disclosure.
existing_material_to_reuse: Week 1 / Day 1 / Call opening: Greeting and the call recording disclosure.

knowledge_check.question: The call recording disclosure prompt does not appear in the tool at the start of a call. What do you do?
options: A) Skip the disclosure because the tool did not ask for it
B) Read the required recording disclosure from the quick-reference card, then report the missing prompt
C) Mention the recording at the end of the call
knowledge_check.feedback: The requirement is to read the disclosure at the start of the call. The prompt is a reminder, not the requirement.

additional_knowledge_checks.question: When must the call recording disclosure be read?
options: A) After identity verification is finished
B) Only if the member asks whether the call is recorded
C) At the start of the call, before the reason for the call is discussed
additional_knowledge_checks.feedback: The QA requirement places the disclosure at the start of the call, before the reason for the call is discussed.

success_criteria: Reads the disclosure before the reason for the call is discussed
Reports the missing prompt after the call

finding.title: Calls closed without confirming the member understood the next steps
finding.observed: On two evaluations the evaluator recorded that the call ended without the employee checking whether the next steps were clear. In one, the member asked what would happen next and the call was closed without an answer.
finding.root_cause: Both comments describe the closing moments of the call, where the summary and the confirmation were dropped. This may reflect pressure to end calls quickly, but two comments are not enough to say so.
finding.pattern: Two of four employees, once each.
finding.curriculum_note: Week 2 / Day 4 'Communication' covers summarizing next steps and confirming understanding.
finding.confidence_note: Two failed items from two employees. A supervisor should check whether handle-time targets are a factor before coaching.
corrective_actions: Coach a two-sentence close: summarize the next step, then ask the member to confirm it.
Check with the two employees whether call-length pressure played a part.

module.module_title: Close the call: summarize the next step and confirm understanding
module.learning_objective: By the end of this session the employee ends every call by summarizing the next steps and confirming that the member understands them.
module.why_this_fixes_the_gap: Both failed evaluations describe calls that ended without that check. A fixed two-sentence close makes the behavior quick enough to use on every call.
instruction: Use a two-sentence close: state the next step, then ask the member to confirm it.
Say who does what, and by when, in the summary.
Ask an open check such as "What will you be expecting from us?" rather than "Is that okay?".
If the member asks what happens next, answer before closing.
Do not start the closing script until the confirmation is given.
existing_material_to_reuse: Week 2 / Day 4 / Communication: Summarize the next steps and confirm understanding.

knowledge_check.question: Which closing confirms understanding and next steps with the member?
options: A) "Is there anything else? Thanks for calling."
B) "So the claims team will call you by Friday. Can you tell me what you'll be expecting from us?"
C) "You should be all set."
knowledge_check.feedback: B summarizes the next step and checks understanding with a question the member has to answer. A and C end the call without either.

additional_knowledge_checks.question: The member asks, "So what happens now?" as you begin your closing. What do you do?
options: A) Answer the question, summarize the next step, and confirm they understand before closing
B) Finish the closing script, since the call is ending
C) Tell them it is in the notes
additional_knowledge_checks.feedback: A member asking what happens next has not understood the next steps. Closing without answering is what the evaluator scored No.

additional_knowledge_checks.question: Which question best checks that the member understood the next step?
options: A) "Okay?"
B) "Does that make sense?"
C) "What will you be expecting from us after this call?"
additional_knowledge_checks.feedback: An open question lets you hear the member's understanding. A yes to the other two does not show what they understood.

hands_on_exercise.title: The two-sentence close
hands_on_exercise.trainee_instructions: Close three practice calls. Each time, summarize the next step in one sentence and ask the member to confirm it in the next.
hands_on_exercise.facilitator_instructions: Play the member. On one call, answer the confirmation question incorrectly so the employee has to correct the misunderstanding.
success_criteria: Summarizes who does what and by when
Asks a question the member must answer in their own words

simulation_scenario.call_driver: A fictional member calls about a referral that needs approval.
simulation_scenario.member_persona: Sam, fictional member in his sixties, unfamiliar with the process
simulation_scenario.member_emotion: Uncertain: not sure what he is supposed to do next
simulation_scenario.scenario_context: The referral has been sent for approval and the member will be contacted with the outcome. The member does not need to do anything, but is unsure about that.
simulation_scenario.expected_agent_response: Summarizes that the approval team will contact the member, makes clear the member does not need to do anything, and checks understanding with an open question before closing.
scoring_criteria: Summarized the next step before closing
Checked understanding with an open question
Answered the member's question about what happens next

roleplay_script.speaker: MEMBER
roleplay_script.line: So is that everything?

roleplay_script.speaker: AGENT
roleplay_script.line: Almost. Let me summarize: the approval team will contact you with the outcome, and you don't need to do anything until then.
roleplay_script.coach_note: The summary names who acts and what the member does.

roleplay_script.speaker: MEMBER
roleplay_script.line: Okay.

roleplay_script.speaker: AGENT
roleplay_script.line: Just so I know I explained it clearly, what will you be expecting from us?

roleplay_script.speaker: BRANCH
roleplay_script.if_agent_demonstrates_behavior: The member repeats the next step correctly and the call closes.
roleplay_script.if_agent_does_not: The member calls back the next day asking whether he was supposed to do something. Coach note: the close skipped the confirmation.

roleplay_script.speaker: MEMBER
roleplay_script.line: That someone will call me about the approval.

roleplay_script.speaker: AGENT
roleplay_script.line: Exactly right. Thank you for calling.

options.agent_line: Yes, you're all set. Thanks for calling.
options.coach_feedback: The call ended with no summary and no check. Summarize the next step first.

options.agent_line: Almost. To summarize: the approval team will contact you with the outcome, and you don't need to do anything until then.
options.coach_feedback: The next step is stated, including what the member does.

options.agent_line: Just so I know I explained it clearly, what will you be expecting from us?
options.member_reaction: That someone will call me about the approval.
options.coach_feedback: An open question shows what the member actually understood.

options.agent_line: Great. Does that make sense?
options.coach_feedback: A yes does not show what was understood. Ask a question the member answers in their own words.

policy_refresher.summary: The QA requirement is scored Yes when the employee summarizes the next steps and confirms the member understands them before the call ends.
key_points: Both parts are required: the summary and the confirmation.
If the member asks what happens next, the answer comes before the close.
confirm_with_policy_owner: Any required closing statement in the current call script.

coaching_notes.opening: "Let's listen to how this call ended and what the member knew when they hung up."
questions_to_ask: What did the member know about the next step when the call ended?
What gets in the way of the summary at the end of a call?
Which question would you use to check understanding?
what_good_looks_like: A one-sentence summary of who does what and by when.
An open question that the member answers in their own words.
commitments_to_agree: Use the two-sentence close on every call for the next two weeks.

remediation_plan.goal: Every evaluated call ends with a summary and a confirmed understanding of the next steps.
